name: Can an ADU kitchen be designed for aging parents or multigenerational living?

mainEntity.name: What kitchen features make an ADU safer and easier for older adults to use?
mainEntity.text: What kitchen features make an ADU safer and easier for older adults to use?

acceptedAnswer.text: An ADU kitchen designed for aging parents or multigenerational living should focus on ease of use, safety, and comfort. That usually means avoiding overly tall storage, keeping frequently used items within easy reach, and selecting appliances with simple controls and readable displays. Clear walking paths are important, especially if the kitchen opens into a living area or if mobility aids may be used. Good task lighting helps with meal prep and reduces strain, while slip-resistant flooring can improve confidence and safety. A single-level work area and easy-access drawers are often better than deep base cabinets that require bending or reaching. The design should still feel attractive and residential, not institutional. In many cases, the best ADU kitchens for older adults are the ones that look simple, warm, and uncluttered while quietly reducing daily friction. A contractor experienced in custom residential work can help adapt the layout without sacrificing style.
acceptedAnswer.description: An ADU kitchen for aging parents should prioritize easy reach, clear walkways, simple controls, good lighting, and minimal trip hazards. Lower storage, slip-resistant floors, and easy-access appliances can make the space safer and more comfortable without making it feel clinical.
